propositions: Per-pair overlap judgment issues 2N calls (one per candidate per ordering), re-sending the full system prefix each time; batching N candidates into one call per ordering reduces call count to 2*ceil(N/batch_size), eliminating redundant prefix copies.

The hoisted query digest in the system prompt reaches 873 tokens but falls 151 tokens short of the 1024-token cache floor, producing zero cache hits; adding batch protocol instructions to the system prompt lifts the prefix to 1,337 tokens, crossing the floor and enabling caching.

Batching six candidates reduces input tokens from 18,494 (per-pair 8415 baseline) to 9,116 (48% reduction) through call reduction alone; cache hits write 1,331 tokens once then read 1,331 on the second call, recovering an additional 1,331-token saving.

Verdict relation labels shift on 6 of 12 ordered pairs between per-pair and batched builds (conservative drift: five move toward unrelated, one is internally inconsistent and filtered by the both-orderings-agree rule); surfaced findings remain identical; a positive-control duplicate is recovered at full confidence in both orderings.

Batch response demultiplexing must match candidates by their label rather than position; an absent or malformed entry abstains only that candidate; a raising runner or malformed batch response yields an empty result with no exception escaping.
